title: All beings
hook: east, west, north, south, above, below; seen and unseen

segments.voice: Yesterday: sima-sambheda, breaking the barriers: four people, bandits at the door, and no one to hand over. Your line: no one handed over.

A plane at night, and below you the lights of a city. Every little light is a kitchen, a hallway, somebody's night shift. Thousands of lives you'll never meet, all at once, too many to hold one by one. Today, metta stops going person by person. For a week you've practiced with one face at a time. Now the old texts open the window all the way. Every direction. Every being. All of them.
screen: `A CITY AT NIGHT FROM A PLANE.` → `ONE FACE AT A TIME.` → `NOW, EVERY DIRECTION.`

segments.voice: In several Pali discourses, two of them cited today, the same description of the practice appears almost word for word. A person dwells, the text says, with a mind full of loving-kindness, spreading it toward one direction, then the second, the third, the fourth. Then above, below, and all around, everywhere, to the whole world, with a mind that's vast, grown great, without measure, without hostility. East, west, north, south, above, below: a map of the whole world drawn from where you sit. And this step has no faces. You don't have to picture everyone; you couldn't. You let the wish travel outward, like light, with no edge. The Visuddhimagga, the old manual, gives lists to help: may all beings be well, all breathing things, all creatures, all persons. The Metta Sutta, which you'll meet tomorrow, adds more: the weak and the strong, the long and the short, the seen and the unseen, those living near and far away, those born and those still to be born. That last pair means the wish reaches people who don't exist yet. The Buddhist word for this is appamaññā, the immeasurable. Metta is one of four immeasurables, called that because it has no boundary. Not your family. Not your country. Not your species. Everywhere. Of course the mind drifts back to one or two faces. That's fine. Let them be two lights among all the others.
screen: `ONE DIRECTION, THEN THE SECOND.` · `ABOVE, BELOW, ALL AROUND.` · `SEEN AND UNSEEN, BORN AND UNBORN.` · `THE IMMEASURABLE.` · then, large: `EVERYWHERE.`

segments.voice: After a moment of metta for yourself, send the wish out one direction at a time, taking your time with each: in front of you, behind you, to your left and right, above, the sky and whatever's in it, and below, the floors under you and the whole earth: may all beings there be well. Finally let it go everywhere at once, like a light with no lampshade.
All beings. Metta sent in every direction, above, below and all around, without measure.
Your line: everywhere. Above, below and all around, with no edge at all. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: A metta session often ends by extending the wish to all beings in every direction, as the Pali texts describe, often using lists like all beings, all breathing things and all creatures.

guess: every human being on this planet

fork.setup: you're sending metta in every direction, and your mind keeps going back to one face. what do you do?
options: let that face be one light among all the others.
fork.reveal: drifting is normal. the face becomes one light among many, and the wish keeps going outward.

original.note: Pali: the immeasurables, the four boundless states, of which metta is the first.

trapdoor: what you thought: think nice thoughts about the world.
what it means: a wish sent in every direction with no boundary: not family, not country, not species.
what a scholar hears: the stock pervasion formula recurs across the Nikayas (e.g., DN 13, MN 7), and Visuddhimagga IX adds the unspecified and specified pervasions and the ten directions.

sources.ref: DN 13, Tevijja Sutta; MN 7, Vatthupama Sutta: the pervasion of the directions

notes: The pervasion formula is paraphrased, not quoted (Rhys Davids' 1899 wording exists for DN 13 but was not quoted to avoid inexact wording).
The Metta Sutta phrases (weak and strong, long and short, seen and unseen, near and far, born and to be born) are paraphrased from Sn 1.8 and repeated tomorrow; confirm the overlap is acceptable.
